question: If \(r\) is the remainder when each of the numbers \(1059,\) \(1417\) and \(2312\) is divided by \(d,\) where \(d\) is an integer greater than one, then \(d-r\) equals
solution:
When two integers leave the same remainder on division by \(d\), their difference is a multiple of \(d\): subtracting their division equations cancels the remainder. Therefore \(d\) divides both
\[
1417-1059=358,\qquad 2312-1417=895.
\]
It must consequently divide
\[
895-2\cdot358=179.
\]
Conversely, \(358=2\cdot179\) and \(895=5\cdot179\), so the common positive divisors of the two differences are exactly the divisors of \(179\).

The number \(179\) is prime. Indeed, a composite number has a prime factor no larger than its square root; here \(\sqrt{179}<14\), and none of \(2,3,5,7,11,13\) divides \(179\). Since \(d>1\), we must have \(d=179\).

Now
\[
1059=5\cdot179+164,
\]
and \(0\leq164<179\), so \(r=164\). Hence
\[
d-r=179-164=\boxed{15},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
